title: 96-well CTAB-chloroform DNA extraction
author: Lila Fishman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgv6jw9e
materials: Get samples in Costar plates from -80. Remove bottom of Costar base(s) if still in, and place on dry ice (if not moving very fast). Pour liquid N 2 into a small, shallow styro (need a pool deep enough to submerge and flash-freeze tissue). Dip each Costar plate of samples into pool of liquid N 2 , using the silver Qiagen rotor-racks as holders (or similar method to submerge). Replace plate bottoms OR quickly transfer the cold tubes (in order) to labeled non-frozen costar racks with bottoms in place. The transfer of tubes to fresh base is optional, but is prudent IF you collected into strip tubes that were bulk and re-loaded into a used costar base. Very rarely (but distastrously!) a base will crack in the centrifuge or genogrinder, and we think that has to do with brittleness of old and cold plastic bases.

steps.title: Label plates and tube strips
steps.instruction: Pre‑label the front of each 96‑well plate with projectname_plate#, your initials and date; pre‑label the front of each 8‑tube strip with its strip number (1‑12 left‑to‑right) and draw a line on the back of each strip. Verify the project name is unique and that numbers correspond to phenotypic data.

steps.title: Load beads into plate
steps.instruction: Using a bead dispenser with 3 mm cleaned, autoclaved beads, dispense beads into each well of the plate (do not cap the tubes). Align the two perforated plexiglass sheets correctly; do not force the dispenser if it jams and do not use beads of other sizes or damaged beads.

steps.title: Collect tissue into tubes
steps.instruction: With gloves and forceps, place a 2‑pea‑sized amount of fresh tissue (2‑3 flower buds, 1 dense apical bud cluster, 2 folded young leaves, corollas, or side shoots) into each tube, leaving air space below the cap and avoiding compression of the tissue against the beads. Keep samples on a small styrofoam block with ice (or dry ice for >1 plate) while loading, moving one strip at a time. Load in sets of 8, front‑to‑back, left‑to‑right, matching plate map to sample IDs; leave empty wells for dead/missing plants or controls.

steps.title: Cap and store sample plates
steps.instruction: Cap each strip as you go, then lid the plate when full. Transfer the plate on ice or dry ice to a –80 °C freezer (or –20 °C in a pinch) for long‑term storage. Do not load beads onto wet tissue.

steps.title: Prepare CTAB extraction buffer
steps.instruction: In the hood, measure 500 µL CTAB extraction buffer per sample (+8‑10 % extra) into a wide trough or clean tip‑box lid. Add 1 µL β‑mercaptoethanol per 500 µL buffer (for 96 samples: 52 mL buffer + 104 µL β‑mercaptoethanol) and stir to mix. Keep β‑mercaptoethanol in a dedicated L‑200 bottle in the hood.

steps.title: Clamp plates in Genogrinder
steps.instruction: Clamp the plate (or two plates) onto both Genogrinder platforms so that a corner position on each strip is occupied. Do not place a lid on the plate; the strip caps should be snug against the platforms. Optionally add a folded paper towel for cushioning.

steps.title: Grind tissue with beads
steps.instruction: Genogrind at 1500‑1700 rpm (500‑700 rpm, 1× setting) for 20‑30 second intervals, repeating until the tissue looks like pale green wasabi powder (20 s to 2 min total). Do not over‑grind to the point that samples thaw.

steps.title: Add CTAB buffer to tubes
steps.instruction: In the hood, carefully uncap each strip, discard caps into waste, add 500 µL CTAB buffer to each well with a multichannel pipettor, and re‑cap tightly with fresh caps.

steps.title: Brief centrifugation to settle powder
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate briefly at any speed sufficient to pull the powder off the caps and to the bottom of the tubes.

steps.title: Optional second grind for mixing
steps.instruction: If powder remains unmixed, return the plate to the Genogrinder for <5 s at high speed, or gently hand‑mix by flicking or inverting while caps remain tight.

steps.title: Incubate at 60 °C
steps.instruction: Place the capped plate in a 60 °C water bath for ~20 min. Put a brick and paper towel on top to keep caps from popping off. Invert the plate at least once during incubation, then re‑tighten caps.

steps.title: Post‑incubation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Remove the plate from the water bath, blot dry, re‑tighten caps, and centrifuge for 10‑30 s at 4500 rpm to pellet solids.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to new plate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel (or Matrix automatic) pipettor with filtered 1250 µL clip‑tips, transfer 300‑400 µL supernatant from each well to a newly labeled 96‑well Costar plate. If tips clog, bounce gently on the beads; you may need to split each row into two 200 µL transfers. Reserve the original bead‑containing strips for later bead recovery.

steps.title: Add chloroform
steps.instruction: Decant chloroform into a hard‑plastic trough, rinse tips 1‑2× with chloroform, then add 400 µL chloroform to each well of the Costar plate. Recap tightly with fresh caps. Avoid measuring chloroform directly into the trough unless you have a clean graduated cylinder; return excess chloroform to the bottle or waste as appropriate.

steps.title: Mix chloroform and aqueous layers
steps.instruction: Clamp the plate and shake at 0.5× speed on the lowest setting for 5‑10 min, or hand‑invert for 5 min, to mix the chloroform and aqueous phases. Allow tubes to cool to room temperature before recapping if they are still warm.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 5 min at 4500 rpm to separate the upper aqueous layer from the lower chloroform layer.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous layer to fresh strips
steps.instruction: Set up a cut‑down Costar rack to view the interface. Using fresh filtered tips, carefully pipet the aqueous layer (up to 300 µL) from each well into a matching empty strip‑tube. Discard chloroform waste in a separate plate. Avoid drawing up the interface or chloroform. If any gunk is transferred, re‑centrifuge and repeat for those wells.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL cold 100 % isopropanol to each aqueous sample, cap tightly, and invert the plate once or twice to mix. Place the plate at –20 °C for at least 30 min (or overnight).

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 5‑10 min at 4500 rpm. A greyish gelatinous pellet should be visible at the bottom of each tube.

steps.title: Remove isopropanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Uncap strips (caps may be reused if desired). Tilt each strip and pour off the isopropanol into a dedicated waste tip‑box lid, using a trifold towel to wick excess liquid from the open ends. Keep caps in order on a labelled towel if re‑using them.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL cold 70 % molecular‑grade ethanol to each tube, flick to rinse the pellet (or invert to ensure removal of isopropanol), then centrifuge 5 min at 4500 rpm. Pour off ethanol as with isopropanol, wicking out remaining liquid.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Leave the open tubes uncovered at room temperature for 1‑2 h (or overnight) with a Kimwipe over the tops. Do not overdry; stop when the pellet no longer smells of ethanol.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in water
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL ultrapure sterile water to each tube (adjust to 20 µL for low‑yield samples or 100 µL for high‑yield samples). Cap, flick to mix, and let stand at room temperature for at least 1 h (or refrigerate if used within a few weeks). Store the final DNA at –20 °C or –80 °C; do not freeze before the pellet is fully resuspended.
